subject: Polaris Dedicated: fleet-signal & token-mix deep-dive
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <priya@polarishealth.tech>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@polarishealth.tech>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Polaris Dedicated: fleet-signal & token-mix deep-dive

Hi Priya / Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To finish sizing the dedicated fleet for the Polaris pilot, we need a short, structured traffic profile so engineering can produce an initial fleet footprint and cost estimate. If you can paste numbers into the CSV attached (polaris_token_profile.csv) that’s ideal — below is the specific signal we need.

1) Traffic envelope
- Average requests per second (QPS) sustained (business hours):
- Peak QPS (5-minute peak during morning batch / day):
- Peak day multiplier vs average (e.g., 4x):
- Expected seasonal/weekly patterns (brief):

2) Session and concurrency characteristics
- Typical session length (turns/messages) and median/mean:
- Average concurrent sessions (steady state) and expected peak concurrent sessions:
- Percent of sessions that are long-lived (>=30 minutes):

3) Prompt/response token distribution (per request)
- Median prompt tokens, 90th, 99th:
- Median response tokens, 90th, 99th:
- Percent of requests that are function/tool calls or include embeddings:

4) Real-time constraints and tail tolerance
- P95 / P99 latency targets (ms) for inference per user-facing request:
- Acceptable token-generation tails (seconds) and fallback policy ideas:

5) Workload split
- Percent split by model family / capability (e.g., instruction model 60%, smaller reranker 20%, embeddings 20%):
- Any requests that require KV-cache affinity / session pinning? (yes/no)

6) Caching and reuse
- Expected cache hit rate for prefix/KV caching:
- Percent of requests that include repetitive prompts / templates:

7) Security / retention notes
- Data residency or retention constraints we should know about:

If you can populate the CSV and return it, we’ll run a short simulation and send a proposed dedicated-footprint (GPU counts by SKUs), canary rollout plan, and cost delta vs hosted usage.

Timeline: if we get the CSV by end-of-week, we can turn around a pilot proposal by next Wednesday.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Pre-Sales
Redwood Inference

On Thu, 25 Feb 2027 at 11:08 AM Priya Menon <priya@polarishealth.tech> wrote:
> From: Priya Menon <priya@polarishealth.tech>
> To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
> Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:08:00 -0800
> Subject: Re: Polaris Dedicated: fleet-signal & token-mix deep-dive
>
> Hi Jonas — attaching an initial export (polaris_token_profile.csv). I populated the fields we discussed with averages and percentiles from our telemetry team. High-level notes:
> - Avg QPS (business hrs): 28
> - Peak QPS (5-minute): 220 (happens during 08:00–09:30 ET burst window when claims ingestion runs)
> - Peak day multiplier: ~6x (month-end reconciliation days spike more)
> - Typical session turns: 2.8 (median 2, mean 3.1)
> - Median prompt tokens: 45; 90th: 160; 99th: 980
> - Median response tokens: 60; 90th: 420; 99th: 2500 (rare long summaries)
> - Function/tool calls: ~12% of requests (primarily lookup and billing APIs)
> - Embeddings batch jobs: nightly batches of ~100k with 1–2 hour windows (we’d prefer those on dedicated batch nodes)
> - Session affinity: yes — ~22% of sessions benefit from KV cache (chatty workflows)
> - Cache hit estimate: 28%
>
> I left the per-model split blank (we’re still tagging models in the pipeline), but the attached CSV has the raw token-length distributions and a short sample of request types. Let us know what additional granularity you need and we’ll try to add it.
>
> Best,
>Priya
>Priya Menon
>Director, Applied ML
>Polaris HealthTech
>Attachment: polaris_token_profile.csv (csv, 45KB)

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <priya@polarishealth.tech>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Polaris Dedicated: fleet-signal & token-mix deep-dive

Thanks Priya — very helpful. A few follow-ups so our simulation can be more precise:

- Can you replace the blank per-model split with rough percentages (even best-effort): instruction/generation vs rerankers vs embeddings vs retrieval models. We use that to allocate GPU SKUs.
- For the 99th response tokens (2,500) — is that due to a small subset of report-generation requests? If so, can you give an approximate fraction of requests that look like that (e.g., 0.3%)? Those outliers change memory sizing and KV cache kick behavior.
- For function calls: are they synchronous user-facing calls (tight latency SLA) or asynchronous backend calls we could route to a lower-priority tier?
- Nightly embeddings: what is acceptable time window for those jobs? If 1–2 hours isn’t strict we can recommend sending them to a burstable batch pool instead of consuming steady capacity.
- Retention/residency: does Polaris require all inference logs to stay in region for 90+ days? If so we’ll note that on the Private plan.

I’ve attached a short product-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx — please paste the model-split and the fraction of long-summary requests there. If you can return it, we’ll run two sizing scenarios (conservative and optimized) and propose a canary plan (4 GPU pilot, 24–48 hour stress windows).

Quick note on caching: with a 28% hit rate and 22% session-affinity, we’ll likely recommend enabling aggressive prefix caching for the chatty cohort and a small reserved KV cache per instance to lower per-token p99.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: product-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (excel, 120KB)

---

> Hi Marissa / team —
>
> Thanks — attached the completed template (we filled the per-model split and indicated long-summary frequency). A couple quick clarifications:
> - Long summaries are ~0.4% of live requests (generated from the claims reconciliation flow)
> - Nightly embedding window is flexible; we can extend to 4 hours if that reduces impact to steady capacity
> - Function calls are synchronous and need p95 < 350ms end-to-end (user-facing)
>
> We’d like to schedule a 30-min technical sync next week to review the proposed footprint and the canary plan. Are you available Tue 03/02 or Wed 03/03 (ET)?
>
> I’ve also looped in contracts@polarishealth.tech — we may move quickly once pilot sizing looks good.
>
> Best,
>Sam
